checks.ref: command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh; if grep -n '^[[:space:]]*- \[ \]' "$change/tasks.md"; then echo "the tasks listed above are open again - the fix-code stage must leave tasks.md as implement left it"; exit 1; fi

command:start=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "task" && $4 == "started" { print $1; exit }'); base=$(git rev-parse "$start^" 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD origin/main 2>/dev/null) || { echo "cannot tell where this task branch started: no 'gnomish: task started' commit and no origin/main"; exit 1; }; oversized=$({ git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM "$base" -- packages/client/src; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard packages/client/src; } | sort -u | while read -r file; do [ -f "$file" ] && lines=$(wc -l < "$file") && [ "$lines" -gt 300 ] && echo "$file: $lines lines"; done); [ -z "$oversized" ] || { echo "$oversized"; echo "these files exceed the 300-line hard cap - split them, see .claude/rules/process-invariants.md"; exit 1; }

command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
since=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "round" && $4 !~ /^fix-code#/ { print $1; exit }')
start=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "task" && $4 == "started" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$since" ] || since=$(git rev-parse "$start^" 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
changed=$({ git diff --name-only "$since"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
outside=$(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep . | grep -E -v '^(packages/client/|docs/)' | grep -vxF "$reports/review-code.md" | grep -v "^$reports/handoff/" || true)
outside=$(printf '%s\n' "$outside" $(printf '%s\n' "$changed" | grep '^docs/adr/') | grep . || true)
[ -z "$outside" ] || { echo "$outside"; echo "the fix-code stage edits only packages/client/, docs/ outside docs/adr/, $reports/handoff/ and the resolutions in $reports/review-code.md - restore the files above with: git checkout $since -- <file>"; exit 1; }

command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
for patch in "$reports"/handoff/*.patch; do
  [ -e "$patch" ] || continue
  git apply --check "$patch" || { echo "$patch does not apply to the branch - regenerate it as .gnomish/stages/specify/handoff.md describes"; exit 1; }
done

command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
since=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "round" && $4 !~ /^fix-code#/ { print $1; exit }')
start=$(git log --format='%H %s' | awk '$2 == "gnomish:" && $3 == "task" && $4 == "started" { print $1; exit }')
[ -n "$since" ] || since=$(git rev-parse "$start^" 2>/dev/null || git merge-base HEAD origin/main)
review="$reports/review-code.md"
hunks=$(git diff -U0 "$since" -- "$review" | grep -E '^[-+]' | grep -vE '^(---|\+\+\+) ' || true)
removed=$(printf '%s\n' "$hunks" | grep -E '^-' | grep -vxF -- '-- Status: open' || true)
added=$(printf '%s\n' "$hunks" | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+(- Status: |- Resolution: |  +[^ ])' || true)
[ -z "$removed$added" ] || { printf '%s\n' "$removed" "$added" | grep .; echo "only the '- Status:' lines and the new '- Resolution:' lines (continuation lines indented) of $review may change - restore the rest with: git checkout $since -- $review, then re-apply the statuses"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R5 is rejected as 'not-worth-it' without justification. The change's own tasks.md:9 says 'every new or changed file stays under 200 lines; each task's verification includes `wc -l`', CLAUDE.md says 'Files must stay under 200 lines', and .claude/rules/process-invariants.md allows the 300 cap 'only when splitting would hurt clarity', which the Resolution never argues ('pure churn'). Nine files are still over 200 lines: zone_abbreviations_unit.steps.tsx 291, zoneRulesRelease.errors.test.ts 246, checkAgainstZdump.test.ts 239, compile.test.ts 233, zone_rules_lookup.steps.ts 232, zone_rules_release.steps.ts 221, zoneRulesPlugin.test.ts 216, dateTimeFormatWrapper.polyfill.test.ts 215, truncateToCutoff.test.ts 214. Splitting is cheap and low-risk: split plain test files by describe group, and move steps-file helpers into world modules as the review proposed and as was already done for check.test.ts with checkWorld.ts.
R5's Status 'rejected (not-worth-it)' contradicts its Resolution, which applied part of the fix (check.test.ts split into checkWorld.ts). Fix the remaining files and mark it fixed.
